title: Antipodal sum of an affine Walsh polynomial
statement: Let $n\ge 0$, and let $p$ be a real coefficient family on the subsets of $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$ whose coefficients vanish on every subset of size greater than $1$. For every Boolean vector $x$, the values of its Walsh polynomial at $x$ and at the coordinatewise complement of $x$ sum to twice the constant coefficient: $P_p(x)+P_p(\bar x)=2p(\varnothing)$.
hypotheses_covered: the coefficient family has degree at most $1$
$x$ is a Boolean vector of length $n$
replaced: Let $n\ge0$ and equip $\{0,1\}^n$ with its uniform probability measure; write $\mathbb E$ for uniform expectation. For $S\subseteq[n]$, put $\chi_S(x)=\prod_{i\in S}(-1)^{x_i}$ and $\widehat h(S)=\mathbb E[h\chi_S]$ for real cube functions $h$. Let $P(x)=\sum_{S\subseteq[n]}a_S\chi_S(x)$ with real coefficients $a_S$. Suppose $a_S=0$ whenever $|S|>1$. For every $x\in\{0,1\}^n$, $P(x)+P(\bar x)=2a_\varnothing$, where $\bar x_i=1-x_i$.
